name.value: Bard on the Beach Shakespeare Festival

description.value: Bard on the Beach is Western Canada's largest not-for-profit professional Shakespeare Festival, staging plays and special events in two modern performance tents set against a backdrop of mountains, sea, and sky in Vancouver's Sen̓áḵw/Vanier Park. Now in its 37th season, the festival presents multiple Shakespeare productions alongside related dramas and special events such as improv nights. The Vanier Park site sits directly along Vancouver's waterfront seawall cycling corridor, making it a natural cultural stop for touring cyclists exploring the city's coastline.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms an active 2026 season at Sen̓áḵw/Vanier Park with multiple productions, corroborating the OSM record. The phone number on the website (604.737.0625) matches the OSM value (+1-604-737-0625), but the website footer contact address (BMO Theatre Centre, 201–162 West 1st Ave., Vancouver, BC V5Y 0H6) differs from the OSM address (1695 Whyte Avenue), suggesting the website address is the year-round administrative office rather than the festival site. No explicit mention of bike parking, washrooms, or water refill appears in the fetched content; 'Bard Picnics' is listed as a 'Your Visit' feature, providing positive evidence for food on site.
concerns: Address mismatch: OSM lists 1695 Whyte Avenue, but the website footer contact address shows 'BMO Theatre Centre, 201–162 West 1st Ave., Vancouver, BC V5Y 0H6'. The BMO Theatre Centre is likely the year-round administrative office; the actual festival site address should be verified.
The 'Directions & Parking' subpage was not captured in the fetched content — bike parking details (including any bike racks) may exist there but could not be confirmed.
Name includes '(Summer Only)', indicating seasonal operation; this is consistent with the website confirming a June–September festival season.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Bard on the Beach is a well-established, actively operating cultural attraction at Vanier Park directly on the waterfront seawall cycling route; it is a worthwhile destination listing for touring cyclists visiting Vancouver.
